For $k=\mathbb{C}$ , the identification of $D$ -modules is [KMP21, Theorem 1.2], and establishing such an isomorphism with characteristic $p$ coefficients is a straightforward extension. Matching the central endomorphisms on two sides is the true content, whose proof should be interesting on its own. We briefly highlight the underlying idea as follows.

Consider the Weyl algebra over $\mathbb{F}_{p}$

$\mathcal{D}_{\hbar}(\mathbb{A}^{1}):=\mathbb{F}_{p}[\hbar]\langle x,\partial\rangle/([\partial,x]=\hbar).$

Then due to the characteristic $p$ nature, it is straightforward to check that $x^{p}$ and $\partial^{p}$ are central elements. A more interesting central element is the so-called Artin–Schreier expression,

$x^{p}\partial^{p}=\prod_{i=0}^{p-1}(x\partial-i\hbar)=(x\partial)^{p}-\hbar^{p-1}(x\partial).$

It arises naturally in the following three contexts.

(1)

As described above, quantization of Poisson algebras in characteristic $p$ admit a “large center”: the image of $xy\in\mathbb{F}_{p}[x,y]=\mathcal{O}(T^{*}\mathbb{A}^{1})$ under the Frobenius-constant quantization $\Lambda:\mathcal{O}(T^{*}\mathbb{A}^{1})^{(1)}\to Z(\mathcal{D}_{\hbar}(\mathbb{A}^{1}))$ is given by

$\Lambda(xy)=(x\partial)^{p}-\hbar^{p-1}(x\partial).$

(2)

Let $T$ be the $1$ -dimensional complex torus; then $H^{*}(BT;\mathbb{F}_{p})=\mathbb{F}_{p}[\![u]\!]$ where $\mathrm{deg}(u)=2$ . Then the total Steenrod operation $\mathrm{St}_{p}$ satisfies

$\mathrm{St}_{p}(u)=u^{p}-\hbar^{p-1}u,$

where $\hbar$ is the degree $2$ element of the group cohomology of $\mathbb{Z}/p$ with $\mathbb{F}_{p}$ -coefficient.

(3)

Consider a ( $\hbar$ -)connection over $\mathbb{F}_{p}(\!(z)\!)$ with regular singularity at $z=0$

$\nabla_{z\partial_{z}}=\hbar z\frac{d}{dz}+A(z),\quad\quad\quad A\in GL(n,\mathbb{F}_{p}[\![z]\!]),$

then the $p$ -curvature of $\nabla$ , which is a $k(\!(z)\!)$ -linear(!) endomorphism, has the form

$\nabla^{p}_{z\partial_{z}}-\hbar^{p-1}\nabla_{z\partial_{z}}.$

Our proof of Theorem 1.6 is based on reducing the covariantly constant endomorphisms of the $D$ -modules to Artin–Schreier type expressions.

For the $D$ -module of twisted traces, we show that the image of Frobenius-constant quantization map $\Lambda:\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{X})^{(1)}\to Z(\mathcal{A})$ from the universal deformation of $X$ acts by left multiplication (3.14). The map $\Lambda$ generalizes Context (1) from quantization theory to the symplectic resolutions we consider. The map $\Lambda$ can be described explicitly for the Springer resolution $T^{*}G/B$ [BMR08] and for hypertoric varieties (Coulomb branches of abelian gauge theories) [Lon21]. These are both eventually described by the ring of crystalline differential operators, in which the Artin–Schreier expressions enter in a direct way.

paper.title: 3D mirror symmetry in positive characteristic
paper.abstract: Via the formulation of (quantum) Hikita conjecture with coefficients in a characteristic $p$ field, we explain an arithmetic aspect of the theory of 3D mirror symmetry. Namely, we propose that the action of Steenrod-type operations and Frobenius-constant quantizations intertwine under the (quantum) Hikita isomorphism for 3D mirror pairs, and verify this for the Springer resolutions and hypertoric varieties.
